proposed.title: Preserve missing values through Styler gradient normalization
answers: Why do missing cells get the lowest gradient color when all valid values are equal?
How should background_gradient and text_gradient color NaN cells?
How do I preserve a colormap's custom bad color when vmin equals vmax?
proposed.body:
Symptom: Missing cells receive the lowest colormap color in background_gradient or text_gradient when all valid values are equal.
Root cause: pandas/io/formats/style.py:_background_gradient uses matplotlib Normalize, which maps NaN to zero when vmin == vmax.
Fix pattern: Restore NaN using the original gmap's missing-value mask after normalization, then pass the preserved result to both default and explicitly supplied colormaps so their missing-value color is respected.
Constraints: Both gradient methods must preserve missing-value coloring whether equal bounds arise from the data or explicit vmin/vmax; valid values must retain their normalized colors.
Regression coverage: pandas/tests/io/formats/style/test_matplotlib.py:test_background_gradient_nan_single_value checks both methods and implicit/explicit equal bounds, comparing missing-cell styles across constant and varying columns and against valid cells.
proposed.applies: Styler background_gradient and text_gradient changes involving normalization or colormap application.

proposed.title: Normalize non-interval inputs before Cython interval parsing
answers: Why does IntervalIndex construction raise an expected numpy.ndarray TypeError?
Why does astype("interval") fail on an empty nullable index?
How should IntervalArray handle RangeIndex and non-interval extension arrays?
proposed.body:
Symptom: IntervalIndex construction, astype("interval"), or set operations with an empty RangeIndex raise an uninformative Cython TypeError about expecting numpy.ndarray.
Root cause: pandas/core/arrays/interval.py:IntervalArray.__new__ passed RangeIndex or non-interval ExtensionArray input to intervals_to_interval_bounds, which requires an ndarray.
Fix pattern: Extract RangeIndex with extract_range=True, then convert remaining ExtensionArray input with np.asarray after _maybe_convert_platform_interval and before the Cython call.
Constraints: Normalize in the non-IntervalArray constructor branch; empty or all-NA input must construct successfully, while populated non-interval input must raise the usual 'is not an interval' error, as checked by pandas/tests/indexes/interval/test_constructors.py:test_constructor_non_interval_empty_or_na and test_constructor_non_interval_raises.
proposed.applies: IntervalArray construction and IntervalIndex construction or interval casts from RangeIndex and non-interval extension arrays.

proposed.title: Keep constructor normalization out of the shared interval conversion helper
answers: Where should non-interval extension arrays be converted to numpy arrays?
Why must from_breaks preserve extension-array breaks?
Can _maybe_convert_platform_interval normalize all extension arrays?
proposed.body:
Constructor-specific ndarray normalization belongs in pandas/core/arrays/interval.py:IntervalArray.__new__.
The shared pandas/core/arrays/interval.py:_maybe_convert_platform_interval also serves from_breaks, which must keep extension-array breaks intact.
Moving this normalization into the shared helper would violate that preservation requirement; retain the constructor boundary when fixing interval-input parsing.
proposed.applies: Changes to interval input normalization that could affect both direct construction and from_breaks.

proposed.title: Empty RangeIndex set operations retain feature-dependent dtype behavior
answers: What dtype should IntervalIndex union with an empty RangeIndex return?
Why does symmetric_difference with an empty index return object dtype?
How does infer_string affect empty RangeIndex set operations?
proposed.body:
For union and symmetric_difference between an IntervalIndex and an empty RangeIndex, the expected result is the original IntervalIndex when infer_string is enabled and index.astype(object) otherwise.
Preserve this contract for both operand orders and across closure and sort settings; ignoring the empty RangeIndex for result dtype is conditional on infer_string.
The regression contract is enforced by pandas/tests/indexes/interval/test_setops.py:TestIntervalIndex.test_set_op_empty_rangeindex; unconditional dtype preservation would break the disabled-infer_string expectation.
proposed.applies: IntervalIndex union and symmetric_difference involving an empty RangeIndex.

proposed.title: Preserve missing MultiIndex column labels in Excel headers
answers: Why does to_excel replace a NaN column label with the last label?
Why did the missing pd.cut bin become (0.0, inf] in Excel?
How should Excel formatting resolve missing MultiIndex column labels?
proposed.body:
Symptom: DataFrame.to_excel writes a NaN MultiIndex column label as the last value of its level.
Root cause: pandas/io/formats/excel.py:ExcelFormatter._format_header_mi resolves missing-label code -1 with positional take, which selects the last level value.
Fix pattern: Resolve MultiIndex label codes with levels.take(level_codes, allow_fill=True), preserving missing labels for rendering through na_rep.
Constraints: Applies when decoding MultiIndex column-label codes containing the missing sentinel -1; it does not call for replacing valid level values. With default na_rep, missing labels produce empty cells.
proposed.applies: Excel serialization of MultiIndex column headers containing missing labels.

proposed.title: Inspect raw Excel header cells when testing missing labels
answers: How do I test that to_excel writes an empty MultiIndex header cell?
Why can an Excel round-trip test hide a missing column-label bug?
How should Excel header regression tests read missing labels?
proposed.body:
Read exported header rows with pd.read_excel(..., header=None, nrows=2) when checking missing labels in a two-level column header.
Using header=[0, 1] forward-fills empty header cells and can conceal incorrect serialized labels.
pandas/tests/io/excel/test_writers.py:TestExcelWriter.test_to_excel_multiindex_nan_column_label demonstrates asserting the raw header rows and accepting merge_cells as a test parameter.
proposed.applies: Regression tests verifying actual Excel header cells for missing MultiIndex column labels.

proposed.title: Forward date formatting options through OpenpyxlWriter initialization
answers: Why does ExcelWriter with openpyxl ignore my date format?
How do I preserve custom date and datetime formats in Excel exports?
What date formatting behavior must openpyxl write and append modes preserve?
proposed.body:
Symptom: Excel exports using engine="openpyxl" ignore the requested date_format and datetime_format.
Root cause: pandas/io/excel/_openpyxl.py:OpenpyxlWriter.__init__ accepted these options but omitted them from the superclass constructor call.
Fix pattern: Forward both formatting options to the superclass constructor so caller-supplied formats reach the writer's formatting configuration.
Constraints: Preserve independent date and datetime options in write and append modes for .xlsx and .xlsm; None retains defaults YYYY-MM-DD and YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM:SS respectively, as checked by pandas/tests/io/excel/test_openpyxl.py:test_date_datetime_format.
proposed.applies: Openpyxl-backed ExcelWriter initialization and date/datetime formatting for .xlsx and .xlsm exports.

proposed.title: Chunk read failures defer to serial CSV parsing
answers: Why does read_csv raise on a valid quoted multiline field?
How should parallel CSV conversion errors be handled?
Why must parallel read_csv report the same error and row position as serial?
proposed.body:
Symptom: A valid CSV with a quoted newline can raise ValueError under dtype= or a raising converter; invalid files can report whichever worker failed first and chunk-relative row positions.
Root cause: pandas/io/parsers/readers.py:_read_csv_chunks splits at raw newline boundaries, so adjacent chunks can independently fail tokenization and conversion when a boundary falls inside a quoted field.
Fix pattern: Catch Exception around the chunk engine read, signal workers to stop taking chunks, and return None after joining workers; pandas/io/parsers/readers.py:_read then reads serially to produce the result or authoritative error.
Constraints: This broad fallback applies to chunk engine reads. Exceptions outside them retain separate handling; pandas/io/parsers/readers.py:_read catches ParserError, UnicodeDecodeError and OverflowError from the parallel helper, while other exceptions propagate.
proposed.applies: Parallel read_csv chunk parsing and conversion, including quoted multiline fields and genuine invalid values.

proposed.title: CSV warnings must survive failures without duplication
answers: Why does read_csv emit the converter and dtype warning twice?
Must parallel CSV warnings still appear when gathering raises?
Who emits warnings when a parallel CSV worker fails?
proposed.body:
Invariant: When a chunk fails and serial parsing takes over, warnings must appear once; enforced by pandas/tests/io/parser/test_parallel_read.py:test_parallel_worker_exception_falls_back_to_serial.
Scope: The same requirement covers warnings from the Python layer during name inference, enforced by pandas/tests/io/parser/test_parallel_read.py:test_parallel_fallback_does_not_repeat_python_layer_warning.
Exception path: A gather error that escapes without a serial read must still emit collected warnings once, enforced by pandas/tests/io/parser/test_parallel_read.py:test_parallel_gather_exception_still_warns.
Consequence: Changing failure handling without preserving these paths can duplicate warnings or lose them when an exception escapes.
proposed.applies: Warning handling during parallel read_csv fallback and escaping gather exceptions.

proposed.title: Parallel CSV success tests must prove the parallel path ran
answers: How do I test that read_csv actually uses parallel parsing?
Why can parallel-versus-serial equality miss a regression?
How should tests force parallel CSV reading on a single-CPU allocation?
proposed.body:
Convention: Tests intended to exercise successful parallel parsing must reject silent serial fallback; pandas/tests/io/parser/test_parallel_read.py:TestReadCsvParallel._read_parallel fails when the internal helper returns None.
Public-path check: pandas/tests/io/parser/test_parallel_read.py:test_read_csv_parallel_vs_serial_large_file lowers _PARALLEL_READ_MIN_BYTES to 1, sets mode.max_threads to 4, and uses _track_parallel to assert outcomes == ["used"] alongside frame equality.
Platform constraint: That public-path test skips WASM because WASM stays serial and the spy sees no parallel call.
Consequence: Frame equality alone can pass after the implementation falls back to serial, leaving the intended parallel behavior untested.
proposed.applies: Tests whose purpose requires successful parallel read_csv execution rather than fallback correctness.

proposed.title: Reconstruct mode values before returning a masked result
answers: Why does Series.mode(dropna=False) raise TypeError for nullable booleans?
How should algorithms.mode return values with a result mask?
Why does DataFrame.mode fail with boolean dtype when missing values are included?
proposed.body:
Symptom: Series.mode(dropna=False) or DataFrame.mode(dropna=False) raises TypeError for nullable "boolean" dtype.
Root cause: pandas/core/algorithms.py:mode returned numeric counting results directly on the masked return path, before conversion back to booleans for BooleanArray construction.
Fix pattern: Reconstruct result values with _reconstruct_data(npresult, original.dtype, original) before returning them alongside res_mask.
Constraints: This applies to the early return when res_mask is not None; preserve the mask alongside the reconstructed values. The normal return path already reconstructs its result.
proposed.applies: Masked results from pandas/core/algorithms.py:mode, including nullable boolean mode with dropna=False.

proposed.title: Preserve raw bytes when hashing mixed-type object arrays
answers: Why does hash_pandas_object raise UnicodeDecodeError for mixed values containing bytes?
How should hash_array handle non-ASCII bytes alongside integers and None?
Why do bytes with trailing NULs hash differently in mixed-type arrays?
proposed.body:
Symptom: hash_array and hash_pandas_object raise UnicodeDecodeError on mixed-type object values containing non-ASCII bytes; trailing NULs can also be lost during conversion.
Root cause: pandas/core/util/hashing.py:_hash_ndarray used whole-array astype(str) in its TypeError fallback, which decodes bytes as ASCII regardless of the requested encoding and can alter their contents.
Fix pattern: Copy the object array, identify bytes with isinstance, stringify only non-bytes elements, and pass the resulting array to hash_object_array with the requested hash key and encoding.
Constraints: Apply this conversion in the mixed-type TypeError fallback. Preserve existing stringification of non-bytes values; bytes must hash consistently with non-mixed inputs, including non-ASCII content and trailing NULs, with categorize enabled or disabled (pandas/tests/util/test_hashing.py:test_hash_array_mixed_bytes).
proposed.applies: Object-array hashing through _hash_ndarray, including hash_array and hash_pandas_object callers.

proposed.title: Restore shared datetime-like frequency only after the combined index is final
answers: Why does changing concat input order lose the index frequency?
Why does constructing a DataFrame from Series lose CustomBusinessDay holidays?
Where should frequency be restored after index unions or sorting?
proposed.body:
Symptom: Reordering inputs to concat or columns in a DataFrame built from Series can lose the index frequency, including a CustomBusinessDay with holidays.
Root cause: pandas/core/indexes/api.py:union_indexes combines indexes pairwise; an irregular intermediate union can drop frequency that inference cannot recover. Sorting in pandas/core/indexes/api.py:_get_combined_index can also drop frequency.
Fix pattern: Validate the shared input frequency against the final values using pandas/core/indexes/api.py:_maybe_restore_freq, called after the special-branch union and after safe_sort_index; reattach the validated offset rather than inferring it or preserving it at every intermediate union.
Constraints: Restore only when the result is a monotonic-increasing DatetimeIndex or TimedeltaIndex with no frequency, every input is one of those types with the same non-None frequency, and _validate_frequency succeeds. Preserve existing frequency; leave nonmonotonic results, mismatched or missing input frequencies, and nonconforming values unchanged. Skipping validation can attach a frequency despite real gaps.
proposed.applies: Index combination for concat and DataFrame construction involving DatetimeIndex or TimedeltaIndex.

proposed.title: Assert frequency separately in index-combination regression tests
answers: Does assert_index_equal verify the resulting index frequency?
How should I test concat retaining frequency when inputs are reordered?
How can a DataFrame constructor test catch lost holiday-aware frequency?
proposed.body:
Assertion: Frequency-sensitive regression tests explicitly compare result.freq with expected.freq after tm.assert_index_equal, which does not check frequency; see pandas/tests/frame/test_constructors.py:TestDataFrameConstructors.test_constructor_dict_of_series_datetimeindex_freq.
Fixture: Combine overlapping ranges in an order that creates an intermediate gap later filled by another input; a CustomBusinessDay with holidays exercises frequency metadata that values alone cannot recover.
Ordering: Cover sort=True, sort=False, and omitted sort as in pandas/tests/reshape/concat/test_datetimes.py:TestDatetimeConcat.test_concat_datetimeindex_freq_order_independent and TestDatetimeConcat.test_concat_timedeltaindex_freq_order_independent. Expected frequency depends on final ordering: nonmonotonic results retain freq=None.
proposed.applies: Regression tests for frequency metadata in datetime-like index unions used by concat and DataFrame construction.

proposed.title: Reject bare CR near the parallel CSV data boundary
answers: Why does read_csv silently drop the first data row?
Why does parallel CSV reading add a junk first row after a quoted multiline header?
When should bare carriage returns trigger serial CSV fallback?
proposed.body:
Symptom: Parallel read_csv silently drops the first data row or adds a junk first row when a bare CR occurs before the data boundary.
Root cause: pandas/io/parsers/readers.py:_read_csv_chunks uses an LF-based data-start offset, but the tokenizer also ends lines at bare CR; the row-count check can miss the mismatch with blank lines or quoted multiline headers.
Fix pattern: Before trusting the boundary, inspect the preamble plus first data line, remove CRLF pairs, and return None from _read_csv_chunks if any CR remains so reading falls back to serial.
Constraints: Apply this guard to the parallel path's preamble and first data line, including skipped rows; preserve CRLF eligibility. This guard does not validate line endings throughout the remaining file.
proposed.applies: Parallel read_csv chunk-boundary validation for large local files, including headers, skipped rows, and the first data line.

proposed.title: Install bar date locators before shared-subplot label hiding
answers: Why do date labels appear on every shared-x bar subplot?
How should bar plots hide inner subplot date labels?
When should BarPlot install dynamic date locators?
proposed.body:
Symptom: Bar subplots with a regular-frequency date index show minor date labels on inner shared-x axes instead of only the bottom subplot.
Root cause: Installing dynamic date locators in pandas/plotting/_matplotlib/core.py:BarPlot._post_plot_logic happens after _adorn_subplots hides shared-x labels, allowing the new locators to redraw them.
Fix pattern: Install the period converter and dynamic date locators in pandas/plotting/_matplotlib/core.py:BarPlot._setup_date_axis, before subplot adornment; this also ensures user-supplied xticks are mapped through the intended converter.
Constraints: Applies to dynamic date axes for regular-frequency DatetimeIndex/PeriodIndex bar plots; shared-x label hiding requires this ordering, while ordinary positional bar ticks are outside this pattern.
proposed.applies: Matplotlib bar plots using dynamic date axes, especially shared-x subplots and user-supplied date ticks.

proposed.title: Reapply date-label styling after bar axis limits change
answers: Why do some bar-chart date labels ignore rotation or font size?
Can a narrow xlim leave minor date ticks without styling?
Why does BarPlot apply axis properties again after set_xlim?
proposed.body:
Invariant: Dynamic bar date axes must reapply rot and fontsize after set_xlim in pandas/plotting/_matplotlib/core.py:BarPlot._post_plot_logic.
Mechanism: Changing limits can create minor ticks that _post_plot_logic_common never saw, including when a narrow user xlim initially left the view without them.
Consequence: Removing the later _apply_axis_properties call can leave newly created minor date labels without the requested rotation or font size, even when locators were installed earlier.
Verification: pandas/tests/plotting/test_datetimelike.py:TestTSPlot.test_bar_plot_date_axis_rot_applies_to_minor_ticks draws the canvas and checks visible, nonempty major and minor labels with both default and narrow limits.
proposed.applies: Rotation and font-size handling for dynamic date axes in Matplotlib bar plots when axis limits can create additional ticks.

proposed.title: Gate compiled regex replacement on the effective string dtype
answers: Why does replace ignore a compiled regex on Arrow-backed strings?
How should regex replacement decide which dtypes can match?
Why must regex replacement preserve NumPy bytes and non-string column dtypes?
Why does a compiled regex do nothing on categorical Arrow strings?
proposed.body:
Symptom: Series.replace or DataFrame.replace silently leaves Arrow-backed strings unchanged when given a compiled regex, although the string spelling substitutes correctly.
Root cause: pandas/core/internals/blocks.py:Block._replace_regex used a literal object/string allowlist for compiled patterns, excluding Arrow string dtypes before replacement ran.
Fix pattern: In Block._replace_regex, obtain the effective dtype through _regex_target_dtype, then require is_string_dtype(target_dtype) and target_dtype.kind != "S". Resolving categorical inputs to their categories' dtype lets compiled patterns reach the same replacement path as string patterns.
Constraints: Applies to Arrow string and large_string, including categorical variants. NumPy bytes and non-string Arrow columns must remain dtype-preserving no-ops. Supported Arrow string columns follow the existing object-upcast path for incompatible regex replacements. Dictionary-encoded Arrow strings, string_view, and incompatible non-regex replacements remain separate defects.
proposed.applies: Compiled regex eligibility in Series/DataFrame replacement, including categorical and mixed-dtype inputs.

proposed.title: Keep clip bounds one-dimensional during operand alignment
answers: Why does DataFrame.clip turn integer columns into object dtype with nullable integer bounds?
Why does inplace clipping fail with an extension-dtype array or Index bound?
What does flex=None mean in DataFrame._align_for_op?
proposed.body:
Symptom: DataFrame.clip with an extension-dtype array or Index bound degrades integer columns to object dtype or raises TypeError with inplace=True.
Root cause: pandas/core/frame.py:DataFrame._align_for_op broadcast the aligned Series bound through _maybe_align_series_as_frame; the resulting EA-columned frame bypassed where's working one-dimensional EA path.
Fix pattern: Preserve the aligned Series operand when flex=None so clipping passes a one-dimensional bound to where.
Constraints: flex=None skips DataFrame alignment checks and Series-to-frame broadcasting; keep broadcasting for flex values other than None. This guard is enforced in pandas/core/frame.py:DataFrame._align_for_op.
proposed.applies: DataFrame operand alignment used to pass list-like clipping bounds to where, especially extension-dtype arrays and Index objects.

proposed.title: Carry the inferred column axis into clip's where operation
answers: Why does DataFrame.clip require an axis for an extension-dtype bound?
Which axis does clipping use when an array or Index bound is supplied without axis?
How should clip pass an aligned Series bound to where?
proposed.body:
Symptom: DataFrame.clip with an extension-dtype array or Index bound and no axis raises ValueError: Must specify axis=0 or 1.
Root cause: pandas/core/generic.py:NDFrame._clip_with_one_bound passed axis=None onward after _align_for_op had converted the bound to a Series aligned against the columns; subsequent DataFrame-Series alignment requires an explicit axis.
Fix pattern: Carry the inferred alignment axis forward: when operand alignment returns a Series and axis is None, set axis=1 before calling where.
Constraints: Apply this inference in the non-Series list-like bound conversion path; preserve explicit axis=0 and axis=1. pandas/tests/frame/methods/test_clip.py:TestDataFrameClip.test_clip_extension_dtype_bound checks column-default behavior and equivalent inplace and returned results.
proposed.applies: DataFrame.clip's conversion of non-Series list-like bounds when the caller omits axis.

proposed.title: Preserve encoding_errors when adapting CSV text buffers to bytes
answers: Why does read_csv raise UnicodeEncodeError on StringIO despite encoding_errors="replace"?
Why is encoding_errors="ignore" ignored for a CSV text buffer?
How should C and pyarrow CSV engines handle encoding errors when converting text to bytes?
proposed.body:
Symptom: read_csv on a text buffer containing an unencodable character raises UnicodeEncodeError despite encoding_errors="replace" or "ignore" with the C or pyarrow engine.
Root cause: pandas/io/common.py:_BytesIOWrapper.read encoded text without forwarding the configured error handler, implicitly using strict handling.
Fix pattern: Forward errors from pandas/io/common.py:get_handle into pandas/io/common.py:_BytesIOWrapper.__init__, store it, and apply it in _BytesIOWrapper.read when encoding text to bytes.
Constraints: This applies to text buffers adapted to bytes for the C and pyarrow engines; the Python engine reads text buffers without encoding them. Preserve the wrapper's default errors="strict". pandas/tests/io/parser/test_encoding.py:test_text_buffer_encoding_errors verifies replacement and omission of a lone surrogate as "x?" and "x".
proposed.applies: CSV text-buffer handling through _BytesIOWrapper for the C and pyarrow engines.

proposed.title: Check hashability before validating Categorical comparison lengths
answers: Why does comparing a Categorical with an iterator raise a TypeError about len()?
Should Categorical equality treat an iterator as a scalar or as elementwise values?
How should Categorical comparisons handle hashable list-like operands?
proposed.body:
Symptom: Comparing a Categorical with an iterator raises TypeError because the iterator has no length.
Root cause: pandas/core/arrays/categorical.py:_cat_compare_op evaluated len(other) before excluding hashable operands from the list-like length check.
Fix pattern: Short-circuit on non-hashability before checking list-likeness and length; hashable operands such as tuples and iterators take the scalar-like path.
Constraints: Apply length validation only to non-hashable list-like operands; mismatched lengths must still raise ValueError. pandas/tests/arrays/categorical/test_operators.py:TestCategoricalOps.test_comparison_with_iterator verifies that comparing Categorical(["a", "b"]) with iter(["a", "b"]) yields all False for == and all True for !=.
proposed.applies: Categorical comparison operand classification and length validation in _cat_compare_op.

proposed.title: Arrow isin fallback preserves numeric types and null matching
answers: Why does Series.isin raise on mixed values with PyArrow-backed dtypes?
How should ArrowExtensionArray.isin handle values PyArrow cannot box or cast?
Should NaN in isin values match an Arrow null or a non-null NaN?
proposed.body:
Symptom: Series.isin, DataFrame.isin, or Index.isin on PyArrow-backed dtypes raises for mixed-type candidates or oversized integers.
Root cause: pandas/core/arrays/arrow/array.py:ArrowExtensionArray.isin can fail during candidate boxing or pc.is_in casting with ArrowInvalid, ArrowTypeError, or OverflowError.
Fix pattern: Keep the Arrow fast path; catch these failures and compare non-null entries through algos.isin. Convert candidates to an object array, but retain the comparison array's native NumPy dtype for numeric types.
Constraints: In pandas/core/arrays/arrow/array.py:ArrowExtensionArray.isin, the fallback applies to these boxing/casting failures. Separate missing candidates before comparison: missing values, including NaN, match only Arrow nulls, never non-null NaN. Skipping this separation changes Arrow membership semantics.
proposed.applies: Membership checks implemented by ArrowExtensionArray.isin, including callers through Series, DataFrame, and Index.
